questions.q: Which set of reagents carries out the Oppenauer oxidation of butan-2-ol to butan-2-one?
options: Al(OiPr)₃ in excess propan-2-ol, acetone distilled off
Al(OC(CH₃)₃)₃ with a large excess of acetone
questions.explain: Acetone is the hydride acceptor, and a large excess of it pushes the equilibrium towards the ketone. Aluminium isopropoxide with excess propan-2-ol is the reverse reaction, MPV reduction.

questions.q: In the Oppenauer oxidation of cyclohexanol, the acetone used is converted into:
questions.explain: A hydride moves from the carbinol carbon of the substrate to the acetone carbonyl carbon through a six-membered transition state, so acetone is reduced to propan-2-ol.

questions.q: Which alcohol is NOT oxidised by the Oppenauer method?
questions.explain: A tertiary alcohol has no hydrogen on the carbinol carbon to transfer as hydride. Propan-2-ol does react, but it just gives acetone, the same compound as the acceptor.

questions.q: Pregnenolone, a steroid with a 3-OH group and a nearby C=C, is subjected to Oppenauer oxidation. The product, progesterone, contains:
options: A saturated ketone with the C=C reduced
An α,β-unsaturated ketone, as the C=C moves into conjugation with the new C=O
An epoxide formed from the C=C
questions.explain: The 3-OH becomes a ketone and the neighbouring double bond shifts into conjugation with it. The method never over-oxidises to acids and does not reduce C=C.
